make.name: Audi
make.description: German premium brand in the Volkswagen Group. Its electric cars run from the e-tron (later Q8 e-tron, ended 2025) through the Q4, Q6 and A6 e-tron and the e-tron GT, plus China-only models and the separate AUDI brand from the SAIC joint venture.

models.name: e-tron GT
models.description: Four-door electric grand tourer built in Heilbronn on the J1 platform shared with the Porsche Taycan. Sold from 2021; the 2025 facelift brought a bigger battery, much more power and longer range.

sources.name: The Charge Port: Audi e-tron GT

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original e-tron GT quattro and RS e-tron GT with a 93.4 kWh gross battery.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift with more power (up to 912 hp in the RS performance), 320 kW DC charging and longer EPA range; US line-up is S and RS performance.

models.name: Q4 e-tron
models.description: Compact electric SUV and Sportback on the Volkswagen Group MEB platform, Audi's best-selling EV, built in Zwickau and (for China) Foshan. On sale since 2021; the drivetrain was upgraded in 2024 and a facelift with more range and faster charging went on sale in Europe in summer 2026.

models.description: Mid-size electric SUV and Sportback on the 800-volt PPE platform shared with the Porsche Macan Electric, built in Ingolstadt. Revealed in March 2024; the US skipped model year 2026 and the 2027 update made quattro standard there.

models.name: Q8 e-tron
models.description: Audi's first series-production electric car, launched in 2019 as the e-tron (SUV and Sportback) and renamed Q8 e-tron with a facelift and a bigger battery for 2024. Built in Brussels; production ended on 28 February 2025 and the plant closed.

generations.name: e-tron
generations.description: Original e-tron and e-tron Sportback with 71 kWh (50) or 95 kWh (55, S) gross batteries.

generations.name: Q8 e-tron
generations.description: Facelift and rename (revealed November 2022): 114 kWh gross battery for the 55 and SQ8, 170 kW DC charging, new 2D logo.

models.name: A2 e-tron
models.description: Entry-level electric Audi on the MEB platform, built in Ingolstadt. Revealed on 7 September 2026, with production due to start in late 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: LFP (50/58 kWh) and NMC (79 kWh) batteries; 423-645 km WLTP per Wikipedia (figures not yet homologated).

models.name: Q6L e-tron
models.description: Long-wheelbase (2,995 mm) China-market version of the Q6 e-tron, built by FAW-Audi in Changchun, also offered as a Q6L Sportback.

models.name: A6L e-tron
models.description: Long-wheelbase China-market sedan version of the A6 e-tron, built by FAW-Audi in Changchun and shown at Auto Shanghai 2025.

models.name: Q5 e-tron
models.description: China-only three-row electric SUV on the MEB platform, built by SAIC-Audi (SAIC Volkswagen) in Anting since 2022; Audi's first three-row e-tron.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Three-row MEB SUV with an 83.4 kWh battery.

models.name: AUDI E5 Sportback
models.description: First car of the China-only AUDI brand (four rings replaced by the AUDI wordmark) from the SAIC Audi joint venture, on SAIC's Advanced Digitized Platform shared with the IM L6. Unveiled at Auto Shanghai in April 2025; production from August 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 100 kWh CATL battery, rear- or all-wheel drive, up to 770 km CLTC.

models.name: Q2L e-tron
models.description: China-only electric version of the long-wheelbase Q2L small SUV, built by FAW-Volkswagen in Foshan from November 2019. Sales had dwindled to almost nothing by 2025 and Q2 production ended in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single front motor with a 38 kWh CATL battery.

models.name: R8 e-tron
models.description: Battery-electric version of the second-generation R8 supercar, shown at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show and built only on customer request in Europe. Fewer than 100 were sold before Audi ended it in 2016.

generations.name: R8 e-tron
generations.description: Two rear motors, 92 kWh battery, limited production.

legacy_notes.note: Q8 Sportback e-tron 55 quattro, MY2024 ($77,800). Legacy model name 'e-tron Q8' is not an official name; DC charging '31' is wrong (170 kW); 'carmodel_ended: current' is stale: production ended 28 Feb 2025.
Q8 e-tron 55 quattro, MY2024 ($74,400, 285 mi EPA). DC charging '31' wrong (170 kW); model no longer current.

First-generation e-tron GT quattro (MY2022-24, 523 hp boost, 249 mi EPA MY2024). Generation 'string' is junk; charging '22' is not the DC rate (270 kW). Superseded by the 2025 facelift; the US now sells only S and RS performance.
First-generation RS e-tron GT (637 hp boost, 249 mi EPA MY2024). Replaced by the RS e-tron GT performance (912 hp boost, 278 mi, $170,500).
SQ8 e-tron (MY2024-25). First-released date 2019-03-01 is wrong (SQ8 arrived for MY2024); discontinued with the Q8 e-tron in Feb 2025.
SQ8 Sportback e-tron (MY2024-25); same issues as row 25.
Q4 50 e-tron quattro, first generation (295 hp, US MY2022-24). Price $49,800 unverified; replaced by the Q4 55 e-tron quattro.
Q4 Sportback 50 e-tron quattro (295 hp, 242 mi EPA MY2023-24). Marked as the model rep but it is a discontinued trim.

Q8 e-tron edition Dakar is a limited EU special edition built on the Q8 55 e-tron quattro (408 PS, 114 kWh), not an SQ8: legacy 496 hp / 718 lb-ft are wrong, and Audi said it would not be sold in the US (legacy lists North America). Claimed on the Q8 e-tron 55 quattro variant.
